Senses.PreferredTarget: the two halls fight over the cat
AlternateTargets: the two halls dispute the cat
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “the two halls fight over the cat.” The exact phrase occurs 30 times in 29 allowlisted texts; expanded forms specify “the east and west halls.” In the Chan record it is the opening formula and a short name for Nanquan's cat case. The monks of the two halls dispute a cat; Nanquan holds it up and says, “If you can speak, I will not cut it,” no one answers, and he cuts it. When Zhaozhou returns, Nanquan recounts the event; Zhaozhou puts a sandal on his head and leaves, and Nanquan says that had Zhaozhou been present, he would have saved the cat. Later records quote the formula before asking what should have been said, composing verses on the case, or giving prose comments. The exact headword names the dispute that occasions the case; it is not a separate event from “Nanquan cuts the cat.” Elsewhere the corpus explicitly asks why Nanquan cut the cat if killing living beings is a major precept, but no occurrence of this exact formula states Nanquan's reason.
Senses.Note: The explicit precept question belongs to the linked cat-cutting family and is anchored under “cut the cat” (斬猫) and “Nanquan cuts the cat” (南泉斬猫), whose headwords it contains. It is not duplicated here as a headword-free occurrence. The corpus alternates the two graphs for “cat” (貓 and 猫) and often adds “east and west” (東西).

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉東西兩堂爭貓兒，泉來堂內，提起貓兒云：「道得即不斬，道不得即斬卻。」大眾下語皆不契泉意，當時即斬卻貓兒子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhaozhou's record preserves the east-and-west-halls opening and Nanquan's demand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉因兩堂爭貓，乃提起云：「道得即不斬。」眾無對，泉便斬之。趙州自外至，泉舉前話，州脫草履安頭上而出，泉云：「子若在，即救得貓兒也。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later recorded-sayings collection gives the full dispute, cutting, and Zhaozhou sequel.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉一日兩堂爭貓，泉提起貓云：「道得即不斬。」眾無對，泉斬貓為兩段。南泉舉問趙州，州脫鞋戴出，泉云：「子在，救得貓兒。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hongzhi Jue at Tiantong Jingde Chan Monastery (明州天童景德禪寺宏智覺禪師語錄), in a case later versified by Hongzhi Zhengjue. The unnamed monks of the two halls are the collective actors contending over the cat; Nanquan Puyuan raises and cuts the cat, and Zhaozhou Congshen later puts a sandal on his head. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel passages do not name the monks of either hall.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: 博山無異大師語錄集要. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Nanquan Puyuan as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南泉禪師因東西兩堂爭貓兒，遂提起貓兒示眾，云：「道得即不斬，道不得即斬卻也。」眾無對，泉便斬卻。
